panels.title: Healthy volumes
panels.description: These three tiles partition the fleet: healthy + abnormal + unknown equals the number of volumes the reconciler tracked in its last completed sweep. Derived from the per-volume weka_csi_volume_health_status series, so it DOES respect the Tenant / Filesystem / Storage class / Namespace / PersistentVolume filters above.

panels.title: Abnormal volumes
panels.description: These three tiles partition the fleet: healthy + abnormal + unknown equals the number of volumes the reconciler tracked in its last completed sweep. Derived from the per-volume weka_csi_volume_health_status series, so it DOES respect the Tenant / Filesystem / Storage class / Namespace / PersistentVolume filters above.

panels.title: Unknown volumes
panels.description: These three tiles partition the fleet: healthy + abnormal + unknown equals the number of volumes the reconciler tracked in its last completed sweep. Derived from the per-volume weka_csi_volume_health_status series, so it DOES respect the Tenant / Filesystem / Storage class / Namespace / PersistentVolume filters above.

panels.title: Probe failures (last sweep)
panels.description: Probes that ERRORED during the last sweep. This is NOT a volume state and does NOT add to the other three tiles - it overlaps them: a failed probe leaves the volume's previous status in place rather than overwriting it with a guess. NOTE: this is the only tile that CANNOT honour the filters above - it comes from weka_csi_volume_health_volumes, which carries no per-volume labels. It is always fleet-wide.

panels.title: Corrupt volumes
panels.description: Volumes whose data is gone or going: the directory or the whole filesystem no longer exists on the Weka cluster. The driver cannot repair these, and any workload using them is already broken. Counted per volume, so a volume with two such conditions is counted once.

targets.expr: count(count by (pv_name) (weka_csi_volume_health_conditions{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name", category="corrupt"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Degraded volumes
panels.description: Volumes that work and whose data is intact, but which the driver cannot fully manage: no quota enforcing their capacity, a quota that disagrees with the PersistentVolume, or no API credentials. Not urgent, but they will not behave as declared.

targets.expr: count(count by (pv_name) (weka_csi_volume_health_conditions{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name", category="degraded"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Unknown / Legacy Volumes (No API Binding)
panels.description: Volumes the driver could not classify - in practice API-unbound legacy volumes, which it cannot inspect well enough to say more. Not data loss, but not verifiable either.

targets.expr: count(count by (pv_name) (weka_csi_volume_health_conditions{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name", category="unknown"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Volume counts by condition
panels.description: How many volumes carry each condition over time, so a problem spreading across the fleet shows as a slope rather than a number that happens to be high now. 'no condition' is every volume the reconciler tracked that has nothing wrong with it, so the series sum to the fleet size. A volume with two conditions is counted under each.

targets.expr: count by (category, condition) (weka_csi_volume_health_conditions{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name"})

count(weka_csi_volume_health_status{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name"}) - (count(count by (pv_name) (weka_csi_volume_health_conditions{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name"})) or vector(0))

panels.title: Sweep duration (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Reconciler sweep latency from weka_csi_volume_health_sweep_duration_seconds. Uses $__rate_interval, never a fixed short window, so it stays valid across scrape intervals.

panels.title: Time since last sweep
panels.description: time() minus weka_csi_volume_health_last_sweep_timestamp_seconds, per csi_driver_name. Looks back up to 6h (a fixed, deliberately generous window, not a rate() window) so the panel can still report a large staleness value if the reconciler has been down for a while, rather than going blank. Green under 10m, orange 10-30m, red beyond volumeHealthMaxAge (30m) — the point at which the reconciler itself starts marking entries unknown.

panels.title: Abnormal volumes
panels.description: Every volume the driver currently reports as abnormal, and why. The reason comes from weka_csi_volume_health_conditions - a volume with more than one problem appears once per condition.

targets.expr: (weka_csi_volume_health_status{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name"} == 0) * on(pv_name) group_left(condition) weka_csi_volume_health_conditions{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name"}

panels.title: Unknown / stale volumes
panels.description: Every volume whose weka_csi_volume_health_status equals -1 (unknown) within the last $value_max_age. Includes volumes the reconciler has not refreshed within volumeHealthMaxAge (30m default).

panels.title: Unhealthy volumes by filesystem
panels.description: Abnormal and unknown volume counts grouped by backing filesystem, so a single failing filesystem stands out.

panels.title: Unhealthy volumes by storage class
panels.description: Abnormal and unknown volume counts grouped by StorageClass.

panels.title: Unhealthy volumes by tenant
panels.description: Abnormal and unknown volume counts grouped by WEKA organization.

panels.title: Condition summary
panels.description: How many volumes carry each condition, and which category it falls into. corrupt means the volume's data is gone; degraded means it works but the driver cannot enforce or manage it. Counted per volume from the per-volume series, so it honours the filters above.

targets.expr: sort_desc(count by (category, condition) (weka_csi_volume_health_conditions{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name"}))

panels.title: Volumes by condition
panels.description: Every volume currently carrying a condition, and which. Independent of the abnormal settings, so a volume can appear here and still show as healthy above - that is the difference between 'not raised to your users' and 'not happening'.

list.name: value_max_age
list.label: Value max age
list.description: How stale a reading may be and still count. The reconciler sweeps every volumeHealthReconcileInterval (5m default) and marks entries unknown past volumeHealthMaxAge (30m default), so this must comfortably exceed the sweep interval or panels will lose volumes between sweeps.

list.name: organization
list.label: Tenant
list.description: WEKA organization the volume belongs to.

list.name: storage_class_name
list.label: Storage class
list.description: StorageClass the volume was provisioned from.

list.name: pv_name
list.label: PersistentVolume
list.description: Optional filter down to individual volumes.
